note: The short tail (RI-LOR03 §1: p10 ~90 words; 'How we lose' 8 — a corpus with no scraps feels curated rather than inhabited). Notes, tallies, a bill of lading, prayer-strips, an inscription on a marker that is under water for most of the year, a page torn out of something, and a piece of marginalia that is the only surviving trace of an argument. Two of these are the only source in the game for a proper noun that appears nowhere else, which is T10's defining move and is deliberately not followed up anywhere.

books.title: Bill of lading, Archon, third mooring
books.author: the bond clerk's hand, countersigned
books.unreliability: Correct in every particular and one of the particulars is a lie agreed in advance by three people, and there is no way to tell which from the document.
books.text:
OUT OF ARCHON, THIRD MOORING. Master: Fell Sarano. Bottom: the Gull of Ebonheart, forty-one tons.

One hundred and nine sacks of salt, coarse.
Six bundles of iron bar.
Four reams of paper.
Sixty-two stoppered jars of dye, vat-fast.
Cordage, as per the yard's note appended, which is not appended.
Sundries personal to the master, one chest, sealed, not opened, per the standing arrangement.

ENTERED at the bond house this day and found to agree with the yard's count.

DECLARED VALUE for the toll: nine hundred and forty.

COUNTERSIGNED: S. Idrano, bond clerk. C. Vaneth, harbourmaster. F. Sarano, master.

In the margin, in a fourth hand, in pencil, rubbed: sixty-two jars went aboard and sixty went on the manifest at Ebonheart. Asked Idrano. Idrano says the manifest at Ebonheart is not our business. She is right that it is not our business.

A second sheet, pinned to the first, in the harbourmaster's hand: the yard's note on the cordage was not appended because there is no yard note. The cordage was counted onto the deck by me and by the master together and came to eight coils, and eight coils is what the Gull carries, and the line on this bill is left open because Idrano will not enter a figure she did not see. This is correct practice and I have told her so and I have also told her that a bill with an open line on it is a bill that gets filled in later, and she said that was their problem and not hers, which is the third time this year.

books.title: Inscription, the marker at the second bend
books.author: unsigned; cut in stone, and under water eight months of the year
books.unreliability: It is a warning and nobody now knows what it is warning about, and it is legible for four months a year in a place nobody has a reason to be.
books.text:
THE WATER IS TOLD HERE AND NOT ABOVE HERE
WHOEVER TELLS IT ABOVE HERE HAS NOT ASKED THE ONES BELOW
AND WILL BE ASKED, AFTERWARDS, BY ALL OF THEM AT ONCE

SHUT WHAT YOU OPEN
COUNT WHAT YOU SHUT
AND IF YOU CANNOT COUNT IT, LEAVE IT SHUT AND GO HOME AND SAY SO

books.title: Prayer-strips, Tideway Shrine, taken from the rail
books.author: many hands, in reed-ink, most of them unpractised
books.unreliability: Anonymous, sincere, and there is no evidence anywhere that anything reads them.
books.text:
A strip is written, folded once, and tied to the rail at the turn of the tide. They are not taken down. The rail carries a few hundred at any time and the old ones go into the water.

For the barge that has not come.

That my brother's hands would be better and that he would stop saying they are better.

Nine. (This one is written nine times on one strip and nothing else.)

That the count at Blackrose would be read.

For Ei-Shun, who is in the Silence, three days.

That I would stop coming here.

For the ones going down, whoever they are, from someone who has been told not to ask and has stopped asking.

That the tree at the third well would say anything at all, one word, to anyone, and I do not care what it is.

For the four hundred and eleven.

That whoever reads these, if anything reads these, would understand that we know it does not work and we do it anyway and that the doing is not a mistake.

books.title: A note, found folded in a boot
books.author: unsigned
books.unreliability: Written to somebody who already knew what it was about, which is the whole difficulty.
books.text:
If you are reading this it is because you have got the boots, which means either I am dead or I have finally sold them, and if it is the second one give this back.

Do not go with the Company. I know what they are paying. I know what they told you about the Lilmoth work and it is true, they did pay it, and a dozen went and nine came back, and the three are not being talked about and the nine will not say the names.

The factor is a decent man. That is the trap. He is decent and he will be decent to you right up until the point where he needs something and then he will be decent about that too.

Go to the quay. Weeja-Sen is short-handed every wet season and she pays late and she pays.

Burn this, you sentimental idiot.

On the reverse, later, in the same hand and a worse pen: I have gone with the Company. Do not be clever about this. The quay work went to a factor's cousin and the wet season is three months and I have counted what I have. If I am wrong you may say so to my face in the spring and I will buy. If I am not wrong you will not have to say anything.

books.title: Yard tally, Blackrose, the fourth quarter
books.author: the yard clerk, and one correction
books.unreliability: Three numbers that cannot all be right, in a document whose only purpose is to be right.
books.text:
UNDER SENTENCE, at the wall, counted at first light on the last day of the quarter: five hundred and twenty-nine.

OUT ON LEASE, per the lease register, this quarter: four hundred and eleven.

TOTAL, per the register of persons: nine hundred and forty.

529 and 411 is 940. Signed and away.

Below, in a different hand, undated: the flats returned three hundred and ninety-four bodies to the gate this quarter and the yard signed for three hundred and ninety-four. The register was not altered because the register counts the lease and not the men, and the lease is four hundred and eleven until the term ends. I have written to the Prefect. This is the second time I have written to the Prefect.

books.title: A page, torn at both edges
books.author: unknown; the hand is a chapter hand
books.unreliability: Torn out of a book nobody can identify, in a hand that is deliberately anonymous, and it is the only place in the province where the name Ixt-Shaneekh appears beside a date.
books.text:
…and the third condition, which the chapter would not accept and which I record because it was offered:

that the count at Ixt-Shaneekh be taken up again, by us, at our own charge, in the ninth year, and that whatever it comes to be entered in the return column and not in a separate book.

The chapter's answer was that we do not keep other people's counts. The answer was given in one sentence and the sitting moved on, and I want it written somewhere that the sitting moved on in less time than it takes to say it, and that afterwards I could get no answer to what the count at Ixt-Shaneekh is a count of, not even from the two who voted.

I have asked at Helstrom. I have asked at Thorn. I have asked a keeper who was polite to me for an hour and then said that it is not a thing anyone is keeping now and that I had better ask whoever is not keeping it.

The fourth condition was…

books.title: Marginalia, in a borrowed copy of the Blessings of the Coast
books.author: two readers, twenty years apart
books.unreliability: The only surviving half of an argument. The book they are arguing with is in the same library and does not know.

contradicts.on: whether the Empire's law reaches the ships out of Tear

books.text:
Beside "No subject of the Empire may be held as property within the borders of the Empire's law" —

First hand, in ink: Morrowind is in the Empire. My mother is in Tear. Both of these are true at once and this sentence is printed by an office that knows it.

Second hand, in pencil, twenty years later and in the same margin: I have found out who wrote this and he is dead and he was a clerk of the fourth grade and he was given the text to set and he set it. The anger has nowhere to go. I have been angry at this sentence since I was a child and there is no one at the end of it.

First hand again, further down, beside "Who has hanged a pirate this year?" — Four. And every one of them off a ship out of Anvil, and not one off a ship out of Tear, and if you want to know what an empire is, that is the whole of it in two numbers.

At the foot of the page, second hand: I am giving this book back now. Whoever has it next, do not add to this. It is finished. It has been finished for twenty years and I have only just noticed.

books.title: Order book, Kiln Camp, the last four entries
books.author: the kiln master
books.unreliability: Practical, terse and it stops. Nothing anywhere says why it stops.
books.text:
Charge the long kiln on the ninth. Fire the tenth at first light. Nine days to the draw and not eight, whatever the Archon factor says, and if he sends the carts on the eighth again they will wait and he will pay for the waiting.

Flues swept the fourth. Second flue is going and will not last the year. Ordered brick.

Brick has not come.

Brick has not come. Fired anyway on the second flue and it drew badly on the west side and the west side of the charge is soft and I am not selling it as hard. Entered as seconds. The factor will argue. Let him.

The hands did not come up this morning. All eleven. I have been to the shelters and their things are there.

(Nothing further is entered. The book is not damaged, the remaining leaves are blank and clean, and the ink on the last entry is the same ink as the entry above it, which the Archon factor's clerk has noted in the margin of his own copy along with the observation that the long kiln was still warm when the carts arrived on the ninth day, as ordered.)

books.title: A receipt, Gideon toll gate, and what is written on the back
books.author: a toll clerk; and somebody else
books.unreliability: The front is a receipt. The back is the only written record of an event that eleven people saw.
books.text:
FRONT. Received at the gate, of one barge, laden reed and hide. Toll at the inland rate, nine drakes. Entered. R. Sath.

BACK, in a different hand, hurried, in charcoal:

fourth day of the wet — the water at the cross went down about a hand between one bell and the next and came back up over the following hour and there is no report from upstream and the tide was at the flood — the whole quay saw it — Sath says it is the sluices at the mill and the mill was not working — writing it here because there is nothing else to write it on and because in six months the whole quay will say it did not happen

books.title: Instructions for the lamp, nailed inside the lid
books.author: unsigned; the maker's hand
books.unreliability: Entirely reliable and slightly frightening, which is a combination only a manual can achieve.
books.text:
Trim before you fill, not after.

The oil is fish and it will not keep past a season in the heat. A lamp that smells sweet has gone and will smoke and will put soot in your lungs, which you will not notice for a year.

Do not carry it lit down a shaft. Lower it lit and follow it. If it goes out on the way down, come up. Do not go down to see why it went out. This instruction has been on this lid since my father made the first of these and it is the only one on this list that has ever killed a man.

books.title: A list of names, on the back of a chart
books.author: unsigned
books.unreliability: Eleven names and no heading. Everything about what the list is for was in the heading.
books.text:
Deek-Ei
Waneela
Marsh-of-Nine
Teeus-Ahai
Sees-the-Weir
Hlaalu Verim
Ashaam
Nine-Toes
Reeh
Ulen Dral
and one more, scratched out so thoroughly that the paper is through

Underneath, in the same hand: this is not the Office's list. I copied theirs and then I put them in the order I would go to them in, and that is the only difference, and if anyone finds this that difference is the whole of what I have done wrong.
